newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Nationalists in buoyant pre-election mood.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Nationalists in buoyant pre-election mood.

text.p: Scottish nationalists launched their election campaign on an upbeat note on Wednesday, encouraged by an opinion poll which showed they had more than twice the level of local support than the ruling Conservatives.

"We are better organised, better financed, and more solidly based than ever before," Scottish National Party (SNP) leader Alex Salmond told a news conference at the beginning of its campaign for Britain's May 1 general election.

The SNP, which supports full independence, is Scotland's second largest party after the main opposition Labour party but is tiny in overall terms, with only four of the 651 seats in the outgoing British parliament.
"Only a real parliament in Scotland can deliver the social and economic policies that Scots want and build a better future," Salmond said.
A poll for the Herald newspaper said support for the Conservatives in Scotland had slumped five points to 12 percent, less than half the level it gathered at the 1992 general election.
Backing for the SNP rose six points to 26 percent while Labour was up one point to 53. The minority Liberal Democrats stayed level at nine percent.
Salmond said a positive SNP campaign based on traditional Scottish values of enterprise and compassion would win a "barrel" of seats, but declined to give a figure.
Labour holds 49 of the 72 Scottish seats at the Westminster parliament with the Conservatives trailing well behind with 10. The Liberal Democrats have nine.

Salmond said the real fight in Scotland was between the SNP and Labour, which is promising a referendum on a devolved Scottish parliament with the right to raise local taxes. The Conservatives oppose any talk of devolution.
The SNP says Scotland could survive as an independent entity since it was a net contributor to the British economy.

"With the Tories (Conservatives) going down to defeat in England, the best possible circumstances exist for the SNP to win the election in Scotland," said Salmond. The SNP is not issuing an election manifesto until next week.
